intro: Hidden activations can drift in scale. Layer normalization centers and scales each example independently, then restores flexibility with gamma and beta.
task: Normalize X over its last axis using population variance, add eps inside the square root, and apply gamma and beta.
requirements: X is a nonempty 1D or 2D array; gamma and beta have shape (number_of_features,).
Use population variance (ddof=0), not sample variance.
Require finite inputs and a positive finite scalar eps; raise ValueError for invalid inputs.
Return a NumPy array with the same shape as X. Do not modify inputs. Test values are moderate.

hints.title: Preserve the axis
hints.body: Compute mean and variance with axis=-1 and keepdims=True so broadcasting stays aligned.

hints.title: Stabilize constant rows
hints.body: The denominator is sqrt(variance + eps), not sqrt(variance) + eps.

hints.title: Apply the affine transform
hints.body: Multiply the normalized values by gamma and then add beta.

explanation: Every row uses its own statistics. Unlike batch normalization, a row's result does not depend on which other examples share its batch.
Population variance divides by the feature count. The task is to normalize the observed features, not estimate a population from a statistical sample.
A constant row becomes zero before the affine transform, so its final value equals beta.
